title: Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Exit Arrangements) Bill 2015
short_title: Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Exit Arrangements) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would create rules for how a Commonwealth authority can leave the Comcare workers' compensation scheme.
Comcare would be able to demand one-off exit payments from departing employers and ongoing regulatory fees from them or their successors.
The bill also streamlines how the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission appoints members and sets premiums to fully cover liabilities.
changes: Comcare can collect exit contributions from former Commonwealth authorities to cover unfunded liabilities.
Comcare can collect ongoing regulatory contributions from employers that have left the scheme.
Employees injured before an employer's exit keep rehabilitation support.
Premium calculations for current authorities must consider fully funding liabilities from Comcare-retained funds and the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
The Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission's appointment processes are streamlined.
Minor contingent amendments are made for the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment Bill 2014.
summary.affected: Commonwealth authorities that leave the Comcare scheme, their employees, and the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission.

speeches.speaker: Brendan O'Connor
speeches.brief: The speaker supported reforms for Norfolk Island and criticised the Abbott government for rushing the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Exit Arrangements) Bill 2015, noting the ACT government announced its intention to leave Comcare on 25 February 2015 and that consultation ended on 8 May 2015, with no need to rush the legislation.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: The speaker opposed the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Exit Arrangements) Bill 2015 and related Comcare bills, arguing they would increase workplace injury risk, remove fair compensation rights, and weaken protections—citing the member for Hinkler's comment that workers could go hang-gliding on lunchbreak as evidence of the government being out of touch, and noting 184 workplace deaths and $60 billion in injury costs annually.

speeches.speaker: Luke Hartsuyker
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988 to require Commonwealth authorities exiting the Comcare scheme to contribute an appropriate amount for unfunded liabilities, protecting employee entitlements and rehabilitation rights without creating incentives to leave. The speaker argued the legislation prevents remaining employers from bearing higher costs and noted the government's technical amendments allow exiting employers to pay liabilities over a longer period.
